## [open-11.0.1] - 2026-11-20

### Added

- `submitKeycloakSignIn` in `playwright-config`, the Keycloak sign-in for an app whose first page has no `h1` ([!21364](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/21364))

- `NullableBooleanFormField` in `typescript-react-ui`: an optional boolean as yes, no or empty ([!21260](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/21260))

- `keycloakServerUrl` in `typescript-react-auth` (local Keycloak for `*.localdev` hosts), `localDevServerHost` in `vite-config` (`VITE_HOST`, rejects every-interface values) and `BindHost` in `ktor-server` ([!21219](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/21219))
- `SidebarNavCategory`, a collapsible sidebar nav item with sub-items, in `typescript-react-ui` ([!21202](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/21202))
- Test support exports `./draft-confirmed-test-support`, `./optimistic-locking-test-support` and `./data-display-test-support` of `typescript-react-ui` ([!21186](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/21186))
- Test support from Commons: `userWithCapabilities` (`typescript-react-auth/test-support`), `QueryClientForTest` (`typescript-react-query`), `./navigation-test-support` (`typescript-react-ui`) and the shared Vitest jsdom setup of `vite-config` ([!21184](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/21184))
- `useServerCheckedResolver` form resolver: Zod first, then a server check of one field, cached for 30 s per query key ([!21180](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/21180))

- `bootstrapObservability` and `grafanaTraceObservabilityConfig` in `typescript-otel-tracing`, and the page frame `AppMain`, `AppMobileHeader` and `AppDesktopHeader` in `typescript-react-ui` ([!21170](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/21170))

- `actionForArchiveState` in `typescript-react-ui`: archive action for an active entity, unarchive action for an archived one ([!21119](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/21119))

- **Breaking** `UserDetails.tenantId` replaced by `tenant: TenantPreview?`; the JSON field is `tenant` with `id` and `name` ([!21140](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/21140))
- **Breaking** `EntityArchiveDialog` takes `messages: EntityArchiveMessages` (`archived`, `refused`, `failed`) instead of `archivedMessage` and toasts every archive answer ([!21120](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/21120))

## [open-10.1.0] - 2026-08-13

### Added

- `GeneratedFileCommentSyntax` and `generatedFileMarker(…)` in `annotations` — the marker line a generator writes into a format that has comment syntax; a format without one (JSON, binaries) gets none. The KSP processors `TypeScriptDefinitionGenerationProcessor` and `TypesListGeneratorProcessor` and the `typescript-react-ui` catalog script write it ([!17072](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/17072))
- `@Generated(by, from)` in `annotations` — a file annotation, because what a generator writes is the whole file: `by` names the generator, `from` the spec an edit belongs in ([!17056](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/17056))
- `Delayed` in `typescript-react-ui` plus `ladleStoryReady`, `isTestMode` and `setTestMode` in `typescript-react-utils` — a story announces when its content stands, so a screenshot is taken of the finished render instead of the loading state ([!17034](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/17034))
- `@Messaging` in `annotations` and the detekt rules `MessagingMustNotReferenceDomain`, `MessagingMustNotReferenceEntity` and `WireNameRequiresMarker` — the messaging layer gets the same guard rails as domain, entity and data view ([!17004](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/17004))
- `PriceWithProfitLine` in the `typescript-react-ui` `conditions-timeline` module — a labelled purchase/selling price pair, used by `ArticleConditionsFormFields` ([!16685](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16685))
- `JsonPath` in `commons/kotlinx-serializers` — the keys to follow into a nested JSON object, in order, as a `@JvmInline value class` over `List<String>`. The empty path addresses the root; every string is a valid key, including the empty one, so there is no invariant beyond the order. `plus`, `isRoot`, `Root`, and `parse(dotSeparated)` — the latter correct only as long as no key contains a dot, which is also why `toString` produces dot notation for messages and not for parsing ([!16659](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16659))
- `JsonObjectPath.kt` in `commons/kotlinx-serializers` — extensions on `kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonObject` instead of a type of our own: `findAt`, `getAt`, `merge`, `decodeAt`, `findAndDecodeAt`, plus `parseJsonObject` and the `EmptyJsonObject` constant ([!16659](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16659))
- `JsonPathDiagnostics.kt` in `commons/kotlinx-serializers` — `describeAlong(path)` says where a path stopped and which keys the level actually has, and `jsonTypeName()` names an element's JSON type. Keys and types only, never a value: a path into a JSON object usually fails over data somebody else owns ([!16659](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16659))
- `JsonObject.atPath(path)` in `commons/kotlinx-serialization-test-utils` — reaches into a nested object in an assertion without unwrapping it level by level ([!16659](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16659))
- `@JsonText` in `units/unit` — marks a string that holds JSON text, which a `String` parameter named `json`, `body` or `content` says only by convention. Named `JsonText` rather than `Json` because the short name is taken by `kotlinx.serialization.json.Json`, and every place worth annotating has that one in scope ([!16659](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16659))
- Invitation handling in `typescript-react-auth`: `captureInvitationTokenFromUrl`, `pendingInvitationToken`, `registerInvitationTokenAxiosInterceptor` and the `OnboardingGate` screen — a token from the invitation URL survives the Keycloak redirect and travels on every request until onboarding is done ([!16607](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16607))
- `UrlPattern.Relative4` in `commons/kotlin-lang` — a relative pattern with exactly four parameters keeps its arity in the type, where `RelativeMulti` carried the same URL but lost the compiler's guarantee that a caller passes as many ids as the pattern has slots ([!16588](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16588))
- `NumberInputFormFieldProps` exported from the `typescript-react-ui` `number-input-form-field` module ([!16523](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16523))
- The building blocks generated code imports: `FileSlot` and the `percentage` renderers in `typescript-react-ui`, `enumTranslationKeys` in `typescript-react-i18n`, `ArchiveFilterRoutingExt` with `ArchiveResult` / `UnarchiveResult`, `RequireIdMatch` and `TracerExtensions` in `rest/ktor-server`, and `MoneyFractionAsCentsSerializer` in `commons/money` ([!16500](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16500))
- Server-generated runtime configuration for TypeScript frontends: the `typescript-utils` entry points `./runtime-context` (`appRuntimeContext`, `deploymentStage`), `./deploy-metadata` (`appGitInfo`, moved out of `typescript-react-ui`) and `./serve-time-injection`, plus `SidebarNavExternalLinkItem` in `typescript-react-ui` ([!16493](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16493))
- `CoreCapability.OperateProduct` in `commons/authorization` — the only core capability that crosses the tenant boundary, so no bundle a user can reach on their own (self-signup, invitation, role change) may hand it out ([!16440](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16440))
- `startOfDay`, `startOfNextDay`, `startOfNextWeek` and `startOfNextMonth` in the `typescript-utils` `date` module — local-midnight period boundaries relative to a supplied reference date. `startOfNextWeek` is the ISO week (Monday), so it does not follow the globally set dayjs locale ([!16437](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16437))
- `useDocumentTitle`, `useAutoPageTitle` and `documentTitle` in the `typescript-react-ui` page layout — the document title follows the rendered page instead of staying on the one left behind ([!16429](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16429))
- `BackgroundJobRegistry` in `commons/health` — the process-wide liveness record of a service's essential background jobs. A job registers with its own staleness threshold and reports started, completed and failed cycles; only a completed cycle resets the staleness clock, and a job that never completed one is measured from its registration. `BackgroundJobName` enforces lower-case kebab-case (it becomes the `job.name` metric label, where a space or a capital makes one alert rule read differently per service) and `BackgroundJobName.of(…)` derives one from a class or schedule label. `GET /health` reports every job (`BackgroundJobDto` in `rest/model`, carrying the last started and last completed cycle so a hang is distinguishable from a dead loop), and `installBackgroundJobs(openTelemetry, backgroundScope)` in `rest/ktor-server` connects a service to its jobs in one call: it publishes the gauges `background_job.stale` and `background_job.seconds_since_last_cycle` (`background_job_stale` / `background_job_seconds_since_last_cycle` in Prometheus) and cancels the jobs' scope when the application stops ([!16415](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16415))
- `Repeating.triggerNow()` — runs a cycle now instead of waiting for the schedule, for work that is normally periodic but sometimes has a reason to happen right away. Triggers coalesce (while a cycle runs, any number of them produce exactly one follow-up), cut a running `errorBackoff` short, and are discarded on a job that is not running ([!16415](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16415))
- `ErrorBackoff` in the new `commons/concurrent` package `it.neckar.open.concurrent.repeating` — `Repeating.errorBackoff(…)` thins out the retries of a job whose cycles keep failing (`exponential`, `constant`) instead of hammering a dependency that is already down at full rate; a completed cycle snaps it back ([!16415](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16415))
- `Repeating.statistics` and `Repeating.state` — started, completed and failed cycles, the consecutive failures the backoff scales with, the last error and the last successful cycle, readable without registering an observer ([!16415](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16415))
- `RepeatingJobs` in `commons/concurrent` — the jobs a component started, cancelled together on shutdown. Thread-safe and idempotent, because `add` runs on the thread that boots the component and `cancelAll` on the one that shuts it down ([!16415](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16415))
- `RepeatingCycleListener` in `commons/concurrent` plus `Repeating.Builder.cycleListener` — observes every cycle of a repeating job (started, completed, failed). A listener that throws is logged, never propagated. `trackedAs(name, stalenessThreshold)` in `commons/health` connects it to the `BackgroundJobRegistry` in one call ([!16415](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16415))
- `selectEntityColumn`, `dateColumn` and `dateTimeColumn` in the `typescript-react-ui` `responsive-table` module — `selectEntityColumn` is the generic replacement for the per-entity `select*Column` functions: a right-aligned link button per row that reports the row through `onSelect` and is disabled while `isSelected` holds ([!16413](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16413))
- `DeployedCommit` in `rest/model` and its resolution in `VersionInformation` — the commit a service was built from, short enough for a badge ([!16406](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16406))
- `extractRoutePatterns` and `renderRouteMapType` in `typescript-react-router` — the route map is derived from the JSX route tree instead of being maintained beside it ([!16401](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16401))
- `articleConditionsTimelineEntryTableColumns` and `toArticleConditions` in the `typescript-react-ui` `conditions-timeline` module ([!16399](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16399))

- **Breaking:** `Repeating` and everything around it moved out of `commons/concurrent` into its own module `commons/repeating`, package `it.neckar.open.concurrent.repeating` — `Repeating`, `RepeatingJobs`, `RepeatingCycleListener`, `stopRepeating`, all `CycleSchedule` implementations and the wall-clock builders. The module depends on coroutines, logging, disposable, annotations, unit and the primitives from `kotlin-lang` and nothing else, runs in explicit API mode, and is documented in its own `README.md`. Consumers declare `Projects.open.commons.repeating` ([!16415](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16415))
- `Repeating.start` is idempotent: a second start on a running job is a no-op instead of an `IllegalArgumentException`, because two callers racing to start the same job is normal and the loser should not fail for something already true ([!16415](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16415))
- `Repeating` decides when a cycle runs through a `CycleSchedule`: `IntervalSchedule` (`Repeating.every`) keeps the existing "first cycle now, then one interval after each cycle finished" behaviour, `RandomIntervalSchedule` draws a pause per cycle so a fleet does not run in lockstep, `ImmediateSchedule` (`Repeating.immediately`) never waits — for work whose own blocking is the rhythm, ended from inside the block with `stopRepeating()` — and `HourlySchedule` / `DailySchedule` / `WeeklySchedule` (`Repeating.hourlyAt`, `Repeating.dailyAt`, `Repeating.weeklyAt`, JVM only) run at a wall-clock time and follow the local clock across daylight-saving changes. Wall-clock jobs therefore get the per-cycle timeout, the error handling and the liveness reporting that until now only interval jobs had ([!16415](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16415))
- `Repeating` lifecycle fixes: a cancelled job can be started again (`cancel` now clears the supervisor job), the supervisor stops instead of restarting the worker forever once the job's scope is cancelled, an error handler that throws no longer ends the loop, and `supervisorScope` defaults to the job's own scope instead of an unmanaged one that was never cleaned up ([!16415](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16415))
- `ArticleConditions` in `business-domain` is an open interface with four shipped implementations — `BareArticleConditions`, `ArticleConditionsWithAccessory`, `ArticleConditionsWithInstallationTime`, `FullArticleConditions`. The implementation belongs to the article type and is pinned by whoever owns the timeline, so nothing is serialized through the interface: no discriminator on the wire or in BSON, no polymorphic registration, and a product module can add its own implementation. The interface declares only what every article has — `part` and `unit`; `accessory` and `installationTime` are declared by the implementations that carry them and are nullable there, because an individual article need not carry what its type may. Each implementation therefore *adds* properties, so `@OpenApiBaseSchema` composes them with `allOf` and the generated TypeScript is a real hierarchy (`type FullArticleConditions = ArticleConditions & { accessory: PriceWithProfit | null; installationTime: string | null }`). The added properties carry no default, so they stay required on the wire and the generated types actually tell the article types apart ([!16306](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16306), [!16360](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16360))
- Everything holding article conditions is generic over the implementation: `ArticleConditionsTimeline<Conditions>`, `ArticleConditionsTimelineEntryEntity<OwnerId, Conditions>`, `ArticleConditionsTimelineSupport<OwnerId, Conditions>`, `ArticleConditionsTimelineEntryView<Conditions>`, `ArticleConditionsTimelineSummary<Conditions>` and `UpsertArticleConditionsTimelineEntryRequest<Conditions>`. `ArticleConditionsTimelineSummary.empty` is a function now ([!16360](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16360))
- The OpenAPI generator builds an `@OpenApiBaseSchema` interface schema from all implementations it has processed — union of the properties, intersection of the required ones — instead of from the first one alone, so every implementation is structurally assignable to the generated base type ([!16360](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16360))
- The OpenAPI example DSL captures the example's full type at the call site; an example of a generic type could be resolved neither to a schema nor to a serializer from its erased class ([!16360](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16360))
- `TestClient.post` / `TestClient.put` take an optional `bodyTypeInfo` for a generic request body; without it an erased generic body now fails with a message naming the parameter instead of a serializer lookup error ([!16360](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16360))
- `articleConditionsColumns()` in the `typescript-react-ui` `conditions-timeline` module carries the part columns every article type has; `accessoryColumn()` and `installationTimeColumn()` only fit a table whose entries declare that part, and `fullArticleConditionsColumns()` is the set for the widest shape. The renderers beneath take the tolerant `ArticleConditionsToDisplay` ([!16360](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16360))
- `toArticleConditions` writes the part alone, `toFullArticleConditions` adds both optional parts, so a page sends exactly the keys its endpoint accepts ([!16360](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16360))

Its timeline table keeps all five columns through `fullArticleConditionsColumns()`, and its upsert form projects through `toFullArticleConditions` ([!16360](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16360))
- `ArticleConditionsTimelineEntry<Conditions>` and `ArticleConditionsTimelineSummary<Conditions>` in `typescript-utils` `conditions-timeline` — the read-side views of the generated entry-view and summary instantiations, which are named after the `ArticleConditions` implementation their article type uses (`ArticleConditionsTimelineEntryViewBareArticleConditions`). ### Fixed

- `rest/openapi-generator` generates a `JsonElement` property as the empty schema (`{"description": "Any JSON value"}`) instead of failing the whole specification with `Currently only sealed interfaces are supported`. A `JsonElement` is any JSON value there is — a value inside a free-form area, where the shape belongs to whoever wrote it — so a discriminated union of `JsonObject | JsonArray | JsonPrimitive | JsonNull` would describe the encoding rather than the value, and the generated TypeScript type stops at `unknown` instead of inventing keys ([!17026](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/17026))
- "Back" on the permission-denied page returns to the previous page instead of reloading the URL that was denied ([!17018](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/17018))
- `FormFieldBase` wraps its control in `FormControl`, so every label points at the id of a control that exists ([!16993](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16993))
- The generated class-names list contains every class once ([!16931](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16931))

- The harvested class spec drops compiler-synthesized properties ([!16913](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16913))
- `hasAnnotation` rejects an annotation class without a qualified name instead of matching it against everything ([!16898](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16898))
- The Playwright report output directories are created including their parents ([!16872](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16872))
- A failed link creation names the file it could not link ([!16871](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16871))
- `WorkingTimesWithPrice.Zero` is a neutral element for `plus` and `minus` — it carries no hourly rate of its own and adopts the other side's, so folding a sum over it no longer fails on the first element ([!16853](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16853))
- `ZippedContainerBuilder` closes the delegate stream when finishing the container fails ([!16831](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16831))

The latter also overflowed at month ends — 31 January became 3 March ([!16437](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16437))

- Detekt bug findings outside Lizergy fixed, among them `NumberFormat` and `DefaultLocaleProvider` in `commons/i18n` and the concurrent and crypt demos ([!16337](https://git.neckar.it/neckarit/neckar-hub/-/merge_requests/16337))
